title: Low-Maintenance Haircuts for Long Shifts and Hard Hats

card_text: Cuts that survive a hard hat, sweat and a twelve-hour shift, with nothing to style before you head out the door.
lede: The low-maintenance haircuts that hold up under a hard hat are short where the headband sits, simple on top, and need no product to look right: a buzz cut, a crew cut, a textured crop or a low taper with a short top. They look the same when the hat comes off as they did when it went on.
If your days run long at a well site, the potash mines or a plant around Carlsbad, here's how to pick one and how to fit the appointment around your shifts.

blocks.heading: Why hard hats are hard on hair.
paragraphs: A hard hat rides on a headband that presses a ring around your head for hours. Hair above that ring gets flattened, hair below it gets pushed out, and by lunch the shape you left the house with is gone.

Add heat and sweat, and anything that depends on a blow-dryer or a set shape doesn't stand a chance. The cuts that survive are the ones with nothing to lose: short where the band sits, and a top that falls back into place with your fingers.

items.title: Buzz cut
items.body: One short length over the whole head. There's nothing for the hat to flatten, and it's dry a few minutes after a shower. Put a fade on the sides so it looks deliberate rather than grown in.

items.title: Crew cut
items.body: A little more length on top, slightly longer at the front and shorter toward the back. Enough shape to look put together, short enough that a hat barely changes it.

items.title: Textured crop
items.body: A choppy top worn forward over tight sides. Hat hair suits it: push the top forward with your hand and the pieces land where they belong.

items.title: Low taper with a short top
items.body: Only the edges come down, so the sides keep some cover under the band. A good pick when work rules or your own taste lean conservative.

blocks.heading: Cuts that fight the hat.
blocks.lead: Sharp at six, flat by noon.
paragraphs: Slick backs, pompadours and big swept tops all rely on product and a set shape. Under a hard hat they flatten into a dent at the band line, and there's no fixing that on a job site.
Long sides run into the same problem. Hair below the band gets pushed outward and sticks out under the brim. Keeping the sides short avoids it.
None of that rules out a longer style for your days off. It just means the cut you live in during the work week should be built around the hat.

blocks.heading: Low maintenance, not no maintenance.
blocks.lead: The edges give it away first.
paragraphs: Short cuts are easy day to day, but they show growth in one place before anywhere else: the edges. The neckline and the hair around the ears blur first, and that's your signal to come back.
How soon that happens depends on how fast your hair grows and how sharp you like it. Ask me while you're in the chair and I'll tell you what I see on your hair.

If a beard is part of your look, book the Signature Cut so it gets trimmed or lined up with the cut. Want it all off? The Head & Beard Shave ({{price:head-beard-shave}}, {{minutes:head-beard-shave}}) takes both down smooth.

items.q: What's the most low-maintenance haircut for men?
items.a: A buzz cut. One short length all over, nothing to style, and nothing for a hat to flatten.

items.q: What haircut works under a hard hat?
